levels.headline: Below the protection threshold
levels.explanation: The covered forecast stays below UV Index 3, the level at which WHO recommends sun protection. This does not mean there is no UV exposure.
actions: Bright reflective surroundings, such as fresh snow, can increase UV exposure.

levels.headline: Sun protection is recommended
levels.explanation: The forecast reaches UV Index 3 or higher. Unprotected skin and eyes can be harmed, and protection helps reduce exposure.
actions: Seek shade when UV is strongest.
Cover skin with clothing, and wear a brimmed hat and UV-protective sunglasses.
Use broad-spectrum sunscreen on skin clothing does not cover; apply it generously and follow its label.

levels.headline: Extra protection is important
levels.explanation: The forecast reaches UV Index 8 or higher, when unprotected skin and eyes can be harmed more quickly.
actions: Seek shade and limit exposure when UV is strongest.
Cover skin with clothing, and wear a brimmed hat and UV-protective sunglasses.
Use broad-spectrum sunscreen on skin clothing does not cover; apply it generously and follow its label.

messages.coverageIncomplete: The forecast covers about {coveredDuration} of this {plannedDuration} outing. Conditions during the uncovered part are unknown.
messages.noElevatedUv: No covered forecast time reaches UV Index 3.
messages.splitExposure: Elevated UV is split into separate periods; the longest continuous period at UV Index 3 or higher is about {duration}.
messages.splitVeryHighExposure: UV Index 8 or higher is split into separate periods; the longest continuous period at that level is about {duration}.
messages.reapplication: If you use sunscreen, follow its label and plan to reapply about every two hours; reapply sooner as the product directs after swimming or sweating.
